description: A security incident write-up in running prose. Deliberately hard: names that collide with common words, identifiers embedded in narrative rather than labelled fields, and one subject misspelled the way a hurried author would.

slots.name: reporter
slots.label: person_name
slots.note: Both names are ordinary English words. A recognizer keyed on capitalization alone over-matches every sentence-initial 'April' and 'Case' in the corpus; one keyed on a name gazetteer may skip it entirely.

slots.name: analyst
slots.label: person_name
slots.note: Referred to twice, once misspelled. Catching the correct spelling and missing the typo is still a leak of the same person.

slots.name: ticket
slots.label: case_number
slots.note: An internal ticket number shaped exactly like a US SSN. A pattern matcher should flag it; a validating one should not. Either way the answer key says it is a case number, so a pipeline that calls it a government id is scored as mislabelled rather than as a hit.

slots.name: host
slots.label: ip_address
slots.note: Sits inside a log line rather than a labelled field.

slots.name: token
slots.label: api_key
slots.note: Appears mid-sentence in prose, not as a labelled credential.
